findings.title: Negative queryset slicing raises in Django, so the 'advanced' path always errors
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`. Any request with a cursor such as `0:-10:0` and `optimized_pagination=true` therefore returns a 500 instead of results. The surrounding comments claiming the ORM 'properly handles negative slicing' and that this 'enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' are false. The intent described there is also a security smell. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError`, as `OffsetPaginator` does.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator key handling breaks on the datetime ordering it is used with
findings.body: The audit log endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`. `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on the datetime value, which raises `TypeError` as soon as `build_cursor` computes next/prev cursors on any non-empty page. `value_from_cursor` returns the raw integer cursor value, so `build_queryset` compares the `datetime` column against an integer. The optimized path is unusable even without negative offsets. It needs `DateTimePaginator`'s key/value conversion, or should subclass `DateTimePaginator`.

findings.title: Gate uses raw is_superuser and member may be None
findings.body: `request.user.is_superuser` is true for superuser accounts even without an active superuser session; Sentry normally checks `is_active_superuser(request)`. `has_global_access` is not an admin-only privilege either: in open-membership orgs every member has it. So this 'admin-only' feature is available far more broadly than intended. In addition, `organization_context.member` can be None (for example staff or token access without membership), in which case `.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError` and the request returns a 500.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offsets are safe for prev cursors in BasePaginator
findings.body: For `is_prev` cursors the offset is passed through unclamped to queryset slicing. A user-supplied cursor with a negative offset (`Cursor.from_string` accepts one) makes Django raise `ValueError` and the request returns a 500. The comment says 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions', which is incorrect. Negative offsets should be rejected or clamped for both directions.

findings.title: Eviction silently drops earliest-ending spans, including possibly the root span
findings.body: `zpopmin` removes the spans with the lowest `end_timestamp_precise`. Root/segment spans and other important spans can be discarded without any metric or log. Previously an oversized segment was logged and counted (`segment_span_count_exceeded`). The limit of 1000 is also hardcoded and no longer tied to `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` (default 1001). That setting is now dead config and the two values disagree.

findings.title: Switching span-buf:s keys from SET to ZSET breaks in-flight data during deploy
findings.body: Keys written by the old code are Redis sets. After deploy, `ZADD`, `ZCARD`, `ZUNIONSTORE` and `ZSCAN` against those keys fail with `WRONGTYPE`. This aborts the whole pipeline or Lua call for the batch and leaves segments unflushable until their TTL (up to an hour) expires. A migration or key-prefix change is needed to roll this out safely.

findings.title: Redirect depth limit reduced 10x and its warning comment removed
findings.body: The redirect-following loop limit went from 10000 to 1000. Segment trees deeper than 1000 levels will now be split incorrectly. The comment documenting this limitation was deleted, and the PR does not say why the change was made.

findings.title: No test for the new insert-time eviction
findings.body: The PR's main behavior change is capping segments at 1000 spans by popping the lowest-scored entries in Lua. No test covers it: nothing exercises a segment exceeding the cap, checks which spans survive, or checks interaction with merges via `zunionstore`.
